official_measurement_examples.name: Marine jurisdiction
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO marine licensing applies in English inshore and offshore waters and can also apply in tidal rivers and estuaries; inland planning boundaries alone do not define marine licensing jurisdiction.

official_measurement_examples.name: Multiple permissions
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO guidance states marine work may also require planning permission, Crown Estate rights, Environment Agency permits, protected-site advice or harbour powers; a marine licence is not a universal project approval.

official_measurement_examples.name: Application timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: MMO aims to decide most validated marine licence applications within 13 weeks but application completeness, consultation and environmental assessments can change timelines.

official_measurement_examples.name: Marine plans
official_measurement_examples.fact: Marine plans are statutory plans guiding decisions in English marine plan areas, but plan-policy assessment is not itself a marine licence or land planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 plan transition
official_measurement_examples.fact: The East Marine Plans fourth report published 14 July 2026 says the plans continue to be replaced with adoption of the replacement planned toward the end of 2027; future plan content must not be treated as already adopted.

official_measurement_examples.name: MCZ current geometry
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's Marine Conservation Zones dataset was updated 13 July 2026 and includes both MCZ and Highly Protected Marine Area boundaries, which must retain designation type.

official_measurement_examples.name: HPMA controls
official_measurement_examples.fact: Marine Protected Area guidance notes HPMAs receive the highest level of protection; an MPA boundary alone still does not determine all proposal-specific consent outcomes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Marine licence, marine-plan compliance, terrestrial planning permission, seabed rights and protected-species licences are distinct controls.

core_rules: marine licensing jurisdiction is not defined by a simple coastline-distance buffer
a marine licence is not terrestrial planning permission
terrestrial planning permission is not a marine licence
marine-plan policy compliance is not a licence decision
a marine licence application is not an issued licence
published decision targets are not guaranteed approval dates
MCZ and HPMA boundaries must retain designation type
an MPA boundary is not automatic refusal for every activity
future replacement marine plans must not be treated as currently adopted
Crown Estate seabed rights are distinct from MMO permission
Environment Agency permits can remain separately required
marine wildlife licensing can remain separately required
marine consent evidence does not determine land or seabed ownership
marine plan evidence does not reserve development or grid capacity
no parcel marine clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MMO, GOV.UK, Natural England and data.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. May-July 2026 marine licensing and plan updates, current MCZ/HPMA geometry and future East Marine Plan replacement were kept distinct from issued permissions.
